conf.description: VMware vCenter vpxd event stream / syslog-raw: the Elastic vSphere integration's pipeline stops at the syslog header for this feed, so this is a genuine Cribl-side positional parser of the bracketed vim.event.* grammar, per direct.cribl recommendation. Tolerant of a variable bracket count since inventory-object brackets (host/vm/datacenter/computeResource) are only present when the event type carries that argument.

conf.comment: vmware-vsphere / vcenter-events / syslog-raw. vpxd renders one line per event as the literal keyword 'Event' followed by the Event object's properties in brackets, then the fullFormattedMessage. UNVERIFIED DISCLOSURE: the work order describes this shape in prose (key, chain sequence, createdTime, eventTypeId, severity, userName, then whichever inventory-object arguments the event carries, then the formatted message) but gives no literal sample line, so the exact bracket delimiter used below ([key] positionally for the six always-present fields; [label: value] or [label=value] tolerant for the variable inventory brackets) is a best-effort reconstruction, not a confirmed grammar. A wrong delimiter assumption means these regex_extract steps match zero events while the pipeline still validates at HTTP 200 -- flagged here and in the README rather than hidden. Validate against a real vpxd syslog capture before production use.

functions.description: document the bracket-grammar assumption and its unverified status
positionally dissect the six always-present core fields (key, chainId, createdTime, eventTypeId, severity, userName) that follow the 'Event' keyword
extract the host inventory-object bracket, when the event type carries a HostEventArgument
extract the vm inventory-object bracket, when the event type carries a VmEventArgument
extract the datacenter inventory-object bracket, when present
extract the computeResource inventory-object bracket, when present
extract the client-address bracket present on session events
extract the client-string bracket present on session events
extract the permission-target bracket present on PermissionAddedEvent/PermissionUpdatedEvent/PermissionRemovedEvent
extract the role-name bracket present on permission events
extract the group-flag bracket present on permission events
capture the fullFormattedMessage as the free-text remainder after the last bracket to end of line
set _time from the event's own createdTime bracket (constraint 1: never target @timestamp directly) rather than the syslog header emit time

per direct.cribl: emit eventTypeId to event.code and the formatted message to message, split the DOMAIN\user userName into user.name/user.domain low-side, translate the error/warning/info/user severity vocabulary through a lookup into numeric event.severity while carrying 'user' as its own flag, lift each inventory-object bracket to its ECS or custom target, and tag the dataset
